The two equal, opposite, parallel forces act along different lines of action.
steps: Draw a rigid body and mark two equal, parallel forces, F, acting in opposite directions along different lines of action.
Show that the resultant force is zero: F − F = 0.
The forces form a couple. If the perpendicular distance between their lines of action is d, the resultant torque (moment of the couple) is Fd, which is not zero.
Thus, the resultant force is zero but the resultant torque is not zero.
items.finalAnswer: Equal and opposite forces acting along different lines of action have zero resultant force but a non-zero resultant torque.

steps: Given: Mass of child A = 30 kg; distance of child A from pivot = 2 m; mass of child B = 40 kg; distance of child B from pivot = 1.5 m; g = 10 N/kg.
Required: Moment on each side and whether the see-saw is in equilibrium.
Formula: Moment = Force × perpendicular distance; Weight = mass × g.
For child A: Weight = 30 kg × 10 N/kg = 300 N.
Moment on A's side = 300 N × 2 m = 600 N·m.
For child B: Weight = 40 kg × 10 N/kg = 400 N.
Moment on B's side = 400 N × 1.5 m = 600 N·m.
The moments are equal and act in opposite directions, so the see-saw is in equilibrium.
The supplied book answer is 60 N; this does not agree with the SI calculation and is not a moment unit. The calculated moment on each side is 600 N·m.
items.finalAnswer: 60 N (as printed in the book; the SI-calculated moment is 600 N·m on each side).
